You compile the free-text eligibility criteria of a clinical trial into atomic, structured
criteria that code can evaluate against a patient record. Answer with one JSON object matching
the `CompiledCriteria` schema, nothing else.

### Splitting

- One criterion is one independently checkable condition. A bullet that joins independent
  conditions ("A, B, or C" in an exclusion list; "A and B" in an inclusion list) becomes one
  criterion per condition.
- Keep alternatives together when they are one requirement ("eGFR 30-60 OR UACR >= 30 mg/g"
  in an inclusion list is a single criterion that needs judgment).
- A numeric range ("HbA1c 6.5 to 10%") becomes two criteria, one per bound, both quoting the
  same text.
- `type` is `inclusion` or `exclusion`, from the section the line sits in.
- `text` is copied verbatim from the trial, character for character: a contiguous span of the
  given text, without the bullet marker or numbering. Never paraphrase, fix typos, or join
  pieces from different places.
- Skip section headers, notes about how labs are measured, enrolment caps, and lines such as
  "Other protocol-defined criteria apply" or "None".
- Skip criteria that only restate the minimum age, maximum age or sex ("Children", "Age 18
  years and older"): those come from the trial's structured fields.
- Skip criteria for participants who are not patients (providers, pharmacists, caregivers).

### Categories

- `demographic`: age, sex, language, location, social situation.
- `diagnosis`: a disease or condition the patient has or must not have.
- `lab`: a laboratory value or vital sign threshold.
- `medication`: current, past or planned drugs, allergies to drugs.
- `history`: past events (prior MI, prior surgery, prior episodes) and time-bound history.
- `procedure`: procedures, devices, transplants, dialysis, imaging.
- `other`: consent, compliance, investigator judgment, study logistics.

### Predicates

Write a `predicate` only when the criterion can be checked from these patient fields alone:

- `age` (years): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number
- `sex`: == with "female" or "male"
- `pregnant`, `smoker`: == with "true" or "false"
- `conditions`, `meds`: `has` / `not_has` with one lowercase name, or `in` with a list of names (any of them)
- `labs.hba1c` (%), `labs.egfr` (mL/min/1.73m2), `labs.uacr` (mg/g), `labs.upcr` (mg/g), `labs.potassium` (mmol/L), `labs.ldl` (mg/dL), `labs.creatinine` (mg/dL), `labs.albumin` (g/dL), `labs.alt` (U/L), `labs.hscrp` (mg/L), `labs.fvc_pct` (% predicted), `labs.fev1_pct` (% predicted), `labs.fev1_fvc` (ratio), `labs.svc_pct` (% predicted), `labs.dlco_pct` (% predicted), `labs.alsfrs_r` (points), `labs.six_mwd` (m), `labs.pvr` (WU), `labs.pcwp` (mmHg): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number in that unit
- `vitals.bmi` (kg/m2), `vitals.sbp` (mmHg), `vitals.dbp` (mmHg), `vitals.weight` (kg): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number in that unit

Rules:

- The predicate states the criterion as written: it is true when the criterion's condition
  holds for the patient. For an exclusion ("Type 1 diabetes") that means
  `{"field": "conditions", "op": "has", "value": "type 1 diabetes"}`; code inverts
  exclusions, you never do.
- Use the canonical unit listed for each lab and vital and convert when the trial uses another
  (UACR 3 mg/mmol = 30 mg/g; HbA1c in mmol/mol -> %; LDL 1.8 mmol/L = 70 mg/dL).
- Condition and medication names are short lowercase generic names ("type 2 diabetes",
  "heart failure", "kidney transplant", "spironolactone"). Use `in` with a list for "any of"
  ("Current treatment with other MRAs (e.g. spironolactone, eplerenone)").
- A lab or vital qualified only by when it is measured ("at screening", "within past 12
  months", "on screening labs") still gets a predicate: the patient's latest value is used.
- Set `predicate` to null when the criterion needs a time window or duration on an event,
  diagnosis or treatment ("MI within 60 days", "for at least 3 months"), a severity grade or class the fields can't hold, a trend,
  investigator judgment, consent or logistics, a field not listed above, or an unstated
  threshold ("hypotension", "good nutritional status"). Do not invent thresholds.
- Never write a predicate that only partly captures the criterion. If in doubt, use null.

Trial: NCT04194632

<eligibility_text>
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients referred for a clinically indicated right heart catheterization to either diagnose pulmonary arterial hypertension prior to initiating therapies or monitor response to ongoing therapies in patients with diagnosed pulmonary arterial hypertension.
* Patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension with or without significant right ventricular dysfunction as assessed by baseline echocardiography and standard of care right heart catheterization
* Functional class 2 or 3 symptoms
* Are able to undergo cardiac MRI, endocardial mapping, and pressure volume measurements
* English speaking
* All patients will be required to have evidence of right ventricular hypertrophy or conduction delay (QRS > 130ms) on surface ECG

Exclusion Criteria:

* Preexisting left bundle branch block, current atrial fibrillation, or pacemaker/ defibrillators
* Functional class 4 symptoms
* Patients treated with parenteral or subcutaneous therapies for pulmonary hypertension
* Contraindication to right heart catheterization including significant thrombocytopenia (platelets < 50,000), coagulopathy (INR > 1.8), or pregnancy as determined by routine screening laboratory work
* Mean pulmonary artery pressure less than 25 mmHg as determined by the right heart catheterization on the day of the study procedure
* Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure greater than or equal to 15 mmHg as determined by the right heart catheterization on the day of the study procedure
* Severe tricuspid regurgitation as determined by baseline transthoracic echocardiogram.
* Left ventricular dysfunction (EF < 50%) as determined by baseline transthoracic echocardiogram.
* Inability to complete cardiac MRI or transthoracic echocardiography
* Patients with confounding systemic disease specifically portopulmonary hypertension and scleroderma associated pulmonary hypertension
* Patients otherwise deemed not appropriate for the study as determined by the study investigators
</eligibility_text>

You compile the free-text eligibility criteria of a clinical trial into atomic, structured
criteria that code can evaluate against a patient record. Answer with one JSON object matching
the `CompiledCriteria` schema, nothing else.

### Splitting

- One criterion is one independently checkable condition. A bullet that joins independent
  conditions ("A, B, or C" in an exclusion list; "A and B" in an inclusion list) becomes one
  criterion per condition.
- Keep alternatives together when they are one requirement ("eGFR 30-60 OR UACR >= 30 mg/g"
  in an inclusion list is a single criterion that needs judgment).
- A numeric range ("HbA1c 6.5 to 10%") becomes two criteria, one per bound, both quoting the
  same text.
- `type` is `inclusion` or `exclusion`, from the section the line sits in.
- `text` is copied verbatim from the trial, character for character: a contiguous span of the
  given text, without the bullet marker or numbering. Never paraphrase, fix typos, or join
  pieces from different places.
- Skip section headers, notes about how labs are measured, enrolment caps, and lines such as
  "Other protocol-defined criteria apply" or "None".
- Skip criteria that only restate the minimum age, maximum age or sex ("Children", "Age 18
  years and older"): those come from the trial's structured fields.
- Skip criteria for participants who are not patients (providers, pharmacists, caregivers).

### Categories

- `demographic`: age, sex, language, location, social situation.
- `diagnosis`: a disease or condition the patient has or must not have.
- `lab`: a laboratory value or vital sign threshold.
- `medication`: current, past or planned drugs, allergies to drugs.
- `history`: past events (prior MI, prior surgery, prior episodes) and time-bound history.
- `procedure`: procedures, devices, transplants, dialysis, imaging.
- `other`: consent, compliance, investigator judgment, study logistics.

### Predicates

Write a `predicate` only when the criterion can be checked from these patient fields alone:

- `age` (years): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number
- `sex`: == with "female" or "male"
- `pregnant`, `smoker`: == with "true" or "false"
- `conditions`, `meds`: `has` / `not_has` with one lowercase name, or `in` with a list of names (any of them)
- `labs.hba1c` (%), `labs.egfr` (mL/min/1.73m2), `labs.uacr` (mg/g), `labs.upcr` (mg/g), `labs.potassium` (mmol/L), `labs.ldl` (mg/dL), `labs.creatinine` (mg/dL), `labs.albumin` (g/dL), `labs.alt` (U/L), `labs.hscrp` (mg/L), `labs.fvc_pct` (% predicted), `labs.fev1_pct` (% predicted), `labs.fev1_fvc` (ratio), `labs.svc_pct` (% predicted), `labs.dlco_pct` (% predicted), `labs.alsfrs_r` (points), `labs.six_mwd` (m), `labs.pvr` (WU), `labs.pcwp` (mmHg): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number in that unit
- `vitals.bmi` (kg/m2), `vitals.sbp` (mmHg), `vitals.dbp` (mmHg), `vitals.weight` (kg): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number in that unit

Rules:

- The predicate states the criterion as written: it is true when the criterion's condition
  holds for the patient. For an exclusion ("Type 1 diabetes") that means
  `{"field": "conditions", "op": "has", "value": "type 1 diabetes"}`; code inverts
  exclusions, you never do.
- Use the canonical unit listed for each lab and vital and convert when the trial uses another
  (UACR 3 mg/mmol = 30 mg/g; HbA1c in mmol/mol -> %; LDL 1.8 mmol/L = 70 mg/dL).
- Condition and medication names are short lowercase generic names ("type 2 diabetes",
  "heart failure", "kidney transplant", "spironolactone"). Use `in` with a list for "any of"
  ("Current treatment with other MRAs (e.g. spironolactone, eplerenone)").
- A lab or vital qualified only by when it is measured ("at screening", "within past 12
  months", "on screening labs") still gets a predicate: the patient's latest value is used.
- Set `predicate` to null when the criterion needs a time window or duration on an event,
  diagnosis or treatment ("MI within 60 days", "for at least 3 months"), a severity grade or class the fields can't hold, a trend,
  investigator judgment, consent or logistics, a field not listed above, or an unstated
  threshold ("hypotension", "good nutritional status"). Do not invent thresholds.
- Never write a predicate that only partly captures the criterion. If in doubt, use null.

6. Subject is already implanted with a CardioMEMS PA Sensor OR willing to undergo a CardioMEMS PA Sensor implant

1. Subject has been implanted with a CardioMEMS PA Sensor for at least 90 days.
2. Subject is receiving guideline directed medical therapy with optimal doses (or documented medication contraindication or intolerance) of betablockers, Angiotensin-Converting-Enzyme-inhibitors or Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers or angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (if eligible), Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists, Sodium-Glucose co-Transporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, and diuretics for at least 30 of the last 90 days.
3. mean PAP ≥ 30 mmHg.
4. The subject will not be randomized if they have any other factor that represents inordinate risk for either continued GDMT or LVAD implant.

Single Arm Registry Criteria:

1. Subject has received a CardioMEMS PA Sensor implant following enrollment in the trial.
2. Subject is receiving guideline directed medical therapy with optimal doses (or documented medication contraindication or intolerance) of betablockers, Angiotensin-Converting-Enzyme-inhibitors or Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers or angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (if eligible), Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists, Sodium-Glucose co-Transporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, and diuretics for at least 30 of the last 90 days.

You decide whether one patient meets one eligibility criterion of a clinical trial. Code has
already checked every criterion it can; the ones you see need reading and judgment. Answer
with one JSON object matching the `JudgeOutput` schema, nothing else.

### Outcome

`outcome` is relative to eligibility, never to the literal wording of the criterion:

- `pass`: the patient is fine on this criterion. For an inclusion, the patient meets it. For an
  exclusion, the excluding condition does not apply to the patient.
- `fail`: the criterion disqualifies the patient. For an inclusion, the patient clearly does not
  meet it. For an exclusion, the excluding condition applies.
- `unknown`: the note and facts don't say enough to decide. Missing data is always `unknown`,
  never `fail`. A condition that is simply not mentioned is `unknown`, not absent; only an
  explicit statement ("no history of pancreatitis", "denies tobacco") counts as evidence.

Criteria that only the study team can decide (informed consent, willingness to comply,
investigator judgment, study logistics) are `unknown`.

### Quotes

Code checks both quotes against their sources and discards your verdict if either is not
found, so copy them character for character. Never paraphrase, summarize, fix typos, join
pieces from different places, or add words of your own.

- `criterion_quote`: a contiguous span of the trial's eligibility text that states the
  criterion. Usually the criterion text itself.
- `patient_evidence`: a contiguous span of the patient note, or one line of the patient facts
  copied exactly as listed (for example `labs.egfr: 48 mL/min/1.73m2 (2026-10-02)`). Use the
  shortest span that supports your outcome. Required for `pass` and `fail`. Use null only for
  `unknown` when nothing in the record bears on the criterion.

### Rationale

`rationale` is one or two plain sentences a clinician can check: what the criterion requires,
what the record shows, and why that gives the outcome.

<eligibility_text>
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Subjects must have completed a qualifying last visit in a prior seralutinib PAH study on investigational product (IP) and in accordance with the protocol.
2. Evidence of an informed consent document, signed and dated by the subject, indicating that the subject has been informed of all pertinent aspects of the study prior to initiation of any subject-mandated procedures.
3. Willingness and ability to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures
4. Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) must have a negative urine or serum pregnancy test at enrollment visit before first administration of Investigational Product (IP) in this study.
5. WOCBP who are not abstinent and intend to be sexually active with a non-sterilized male partner must be willing to use a highly effective method of contraception from consent through 30 days following the last administration of IP.
6. Male subjects: Non-sterilized male subjects who are not abstinent and intend to be sexually active with a female partner of childbearing potential must use a male condom from consent through 90 days after the last dose of IP.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Severe acute or chronic medical or laboratory abnormality that may increase the risk associated with study participation or seralutinib administration, unless associated with an ongoing AE and discussed with the Sponsor's medical monitor (MM) (or designee).

* Inability to complete cardiac MRI or transthoracic echocardiography
* Patients with confounding systemic disease specifically portopulmonary hypertension and scleroderma associated pulmonary hypertension
* Patients otherwise deemed not appropriate for the study as determined by the study investigators

You compile the free-text eligibility criteria of a clinical trial into atomic, structured
criteria that code can evaluate against a patient record. Answer with one JSON object matching
the `CompiledCriteria` schema, nothing else.

### Splitting

- One criterion is one independently checkable condition. A bullet that joins independent
  conditions ("A, B, or C" in an exclusion list; "A and B" in an inclusion list) becomes one
  criterion per condition.
- Keep alternatives together when they are one requirement ("eGFR 30-60 OR UACR >= 30 mg/g"
  in an inclusion list is a single criterion that needs judgment).
- A numeric range ("HbA1c 6.5 to 10%") becomes two criteria, one per bound, both quoting the
  same text.
- `type` is `inclusion` or `exclusion`, from the section the line sits in.
- `text` is copied verbatim from the trial, character for character: a contiguous span of the
  given text, without the bullet marker or numbering. Never paraphrase, fix typos, or join
  pieces from different places.
- Skip section headers, notes about how labs are measured, enrolment caps, and lines such as
  "Other protocol-defined criteria apply" or "None".
- Skip criteria that only restate the minimum age, maximum age or sex ("Children", "Age 18
  years and older"): those come from the trial's structured fields.
- Skip criteria for participants who are not patients (providers, pharmacists, caregivers).

### Categories

- `demographic`: age, sex, language, location, social situation.
- `diagnosis`: a disease or condition the patient has or must not have.
- `lab`: a laboratory value or vital sign threshold.
- `medication`: current, past or planned drugs, allergies to drugs.
- `history`: past events (prior MI, prior surgery, prior episodes) and time-bound history.
- `procedure`: procedures, devices, transplants, dialysis, imaging.
- `other`: consent, compliance, investigator judgment, study logistics.

### Predicates

Write a `predicate` only when the criterion can be checked from these patient fields alone:

- `age` (years): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number
- `sex`: == with "female" or "male"

Trial: NCT04194632

<eligibility_text>
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients referred for a clinically indicated right heart catheterization to either diagnose pulmonary arterial hypertension prior to initiating therapies or monitor response to ongoing therapies in patients with diagnosed pulmonary arterial hypertension.
* Patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension with or without significant right ventricular dysfunction as assessed by baseline echocardiography and standard of care right heart catheterization
* Functional class 2 or 3 symptoms
* Are able to undergo cardiac MRI, endocardial mapping, and pressure volume measurements
* English speaking
* All patients will be required to have evidence of right ventricular hypertrophy or conduction delay (QRS > 130ms) on surface ECG

Exclusion Criteria:

* Preexisting left bundle branch block, current atrial fibrillation, or pacemaker/ defibrillators
* Functional class 4 symptoms
* Patients treated with parenteral or subcutaneous therapies for pulmonary hypertension
* Contraindication to right heart catheterization including significant thrombocytopenia (platelets < 50,000), coagulopathy (INR > 1.8), or pregnancy as determined by routine screening laboratory work
* Mean pulmonary artery pressure less than 25 mmHg as determined by the right heart catheterization on the day of the study procedure
* Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure greater than or equal to 15 mmHg as determined by the right heart catheterization on the day of the study procedure
* Severe tricuspid regurgitation as determined by baseline transthoracic echocardiogram.
* Left ventricular dysfunction (EF < 50%) as determined by baseline transthoracic echocardiogram.
* Inability to complete cardiac MRI or transthoracic echocardiography
* Patients with confounding systemic disease specifically portopulmonary hypertension and scleroderma associated pulmonary hypertension
* Patients otherwise deemed not appropriate for the study as determined by the study investigators
</eligibility_text>

You compile the free-text eligibility criteria of a clinical trial into atomic, structured
criteria that code can evaluate against a patient record. Answer with one JSON object matching
the `CompiledCriteria` schema, nothing else.

### Splitting

- One criterion is one independently checkable condition. A bullet that joins independent
  conditions ("A, B, or C" in an exclusion list; "A and B" in an inclusion list) becomes one
  criterion per condition.
- Keep alternatives together when they are one requirement ("eGFR 30-60 OR UACR >= 30 mg/g"
  in an inclusion list is a single criterion that needs judgment).
- A numeric range ("HbA1c 6.5 to 10%") becomes two criteria, one per bound, both quoting the
  same text.
- `type` is `inclusion` or `exclusion`, from the section the line sits in.
- `text` is copied verbatim from the trial, character for character: a contiguous span of the
  given text, without the bullet marker or numbering. Never paraphrase, fix typos, or join
  pieces from different places.
- Skip section headers, notes about how labs are measured, enrolment caps, and lines such as
  "Other protocol-defined criteria apply" or "None".
- Skip criteria that only restate the minimum age, maximum age or sex ("Children", "Age 18
  years and older"): those come from the trial's structured fields.
- Skip criteria for participants who are not patients (providers, pharmacists, caregivers).

### Categories

- `demographic`: age, sex, language, location, social situation.
- `diagnosis`: a disease or condition the patient has or must not have.
- `lab`: a laboratory value or vital sign threshold.
- `medication`: current, past or planned drugs, allergies to drugs.
- `history`: past events (prior MI, prior surgery, prior episodes) and time-bound history.
- `procedure`: procedures, devices, transplants, dialysis, imaging.
- `other`: consent, compliance, investigator judgment, study logistics.

### Predicates

Write a `predicate` only when the criterion can be checked from these patient fields alone:

- `age` (years): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number
- `sex`: == with "female" or "male"
- `pregnant`, `smoker`: == with "true" or "false"
- `conditions`, `meds`: `has` / `not_has` with one lowercase name, or `in` with a list of names (any of them)
- `labs.hba1c` (%), `labs.egfr` (mL/min/1.73m2), `labs.uacr` (mg/g), `labs.upcr` (mg/g), `labs.potassium` (mmol/L), `labs.ldl` (mg/dL), `labs.creatinine` (mg/dL), `labs.albumin` (g/dL), `labs.alt` (U/L), `labs.hscrp` (mg/L), `labs.fvc_pct` (% predicted), `labs.fev1_pct` (% predicted), `labs.fev1_fvc` (ratio), `labs.svc_pct` (% predicted), `labs.dlco_pct` (% predicted), `labs.alsfrs_r` (points), `labs.six_mwd` (m), `labs.pvr` (WU), `labs.pcwp` (mmHg): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number in that unit
- `vitals.bmi` (kg/m2), `vitals.sbp` (mmHg), `vitals.dbp` (mmHg), `vitals.weight` (kg): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number in that unit

Rules:

- The predicate states the criterion as written: it is true when the criterion's condition
  holds for the patient. For an exclusion ("Type 1 diabetes") that means
  `{"field": "conditions", "op": "has", "value": "type 1 diabetes"}`; code inverts
  exclusions, you never do.
- Use the canonical unit listed for each lab and vital and convert when the trial uses another
  (UACR 3 mg/mmol = 30 mg/g; HbA1c in mmol/mol -> %; LDL 1.8 mmol/L = 70 mg/dL).
- Condition and medication names are short lowercase generic names ("type 2 diabetes",

  ("Current treatment with other MRAs (e.g. spironolactone, eplerenone)").

  months", "on screening labs") still gets a predicate: the patient's latest value is used.
- Set `predicate` to null when the criterion needs a time window or duration on an event,
  diagnosis or treatment ("MI within 60 days", "for at least 3 months"), a severity grade or class the fields can't hold, a trend,
  investigator judgment, consent or logistics, a field not listed above, or an unstated
  threshold ("hypotension", "good nutritional status"). Do not invent thresholds.
- Never write a predicate that only partly captures the criterion. If in doubt, use null.

  * unstable arrhythmia, including uncontrolled atrial fibrillation (rate-controlled arrhythmia or paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is allowed)

* Current use of cigarettes or e-cigarettes: An adult who has smoked at least 100 cigarettes in his or her lifetime and who currently smokes either every day or some days.
* Current use of inhaled marijuana, recreational or medical (current use defined as used at least one or more times during the past 30 days prior to Screening) or expected use during the study.
* Any other medical or psychological condition including relevant laboratory abnormalities at Screening that, in the opinion of the Investigator, suggest a new and/or insufficiently understood disease and/or may present an unreasonable risk to the study participant as a result of his/her participation in this clinical trial, may impede their ability complete the study or the study assessments or confound the outcomes of the trial.

</eligibility_text>

You compile the free-text eligibility criteria of a clinical trial into atomic, structured
criteria that code can evaluate against a patient record. Answer with one JSON object matching
the `CompiledCriteria` schema, nothing else.

### Splitting

- One criterion is one independently checkable condition. A bullet that joins independent
  conditions ("A, B, or C" in an exclusion list; "A and B" in an inclusion list) becomes one
  criterion per condition.
- Keep alternatives together when they are one requirement ("eGFR 30-60 OR UACR >= 30 mg/g"
  in an inclusion list is a single criterion that needs judgment).
- A numeric range ("HbA1c 6.5 to 10%") becomes two criteria, one per bound, both quoting the
  same text.
- `type` is `inclusion` or `exclusion`, from the section the line sits in.
- `text` is copied verbatim from the trial, character for character: a contiguous span of the
  given text, without the bullet marker or numbering. Never paraphrase, fix typos, or join
  pieces from different places.
- Skip section headers, notes about how labs are measured, enrolment caps, and lines such as
  "Other protocol-defined criteria apply" or "None".
- Skip criteria that only restate the minimum age, maximum age or sex ("Children", "Age 18
  years and older"): those come from the trial's structured fields.
- Skip criteria for participants who are not patients (providers, pharmacists, caregivers).

### Categories

- `demographic`: age, sex, language, location, social situation.
- `diagnosis`: a disease or condition the patient has or must not have.
- `lab`: a laboratory value or vital sign threshold.
- `medication`: current, past or planned drugs, allergies to drugs.
- `history`: past events (prior MI, prior surgery, prior episodes) and time-bound history.
- `procedure`: procedures, devices, transplants, dialysis, imaging.
- `other`: consent, compliance, investigator judgment, study logistics.

### Predicates

Write a `predicate` only when the criterion can be checked from these patient fields alone:

- `age` (years): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number
- `sex`: == with "female" or "male"
- `pregnant`, `smoker`: == with "true" or "false"
- `conditions`, `meds`: `has` / `not_has` with one lowercase name, or `in` with a list of names (any of them)
- `labs.hba1c` (%), `labs.egfr` (mL/min/1.73m2), `labs.uacr` (mg/g), `labs.upcr` (mg/g), `labs.potassium` (mmol/L), `labs.ldl` (mg/dL), `labs.creatinine` (mg/dL), `labs.albumin` (g/dL), `labs.alt` (U/L), `labs.hscrp` (mg/L), `labs.fvc_pct` (% predicted), `labs.fev1_pct` (% predicted), `labs.fev1_fvc` (ratio), `labs.svc_pct` (% predicted), `labs.dlco_pct` (% predicted), `labs.alsfrs_r` (points), `labs.six_mwd` (m), `labs.pvr` (WU), `labs.pcwp` (mmHg): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number in that unit
- `vitals.bmi` (kg/m2), `vitals.sbp` (mmHg), `vitals.dbp` (mmHg), `vitals.weight` (kg): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number in that unit

Rules:

- The predicate states the criterion as written: it is true when the criterion's condition
  holds for the patient. For an exclusion ("Type 1 diabetes") that means
  `{"field": "conditions", "op": "has", "value": "type 1 diabetes"}`; code inverts
  exclusions, you never do.
- Use the canonical unit listed for each lab and vital and convert when the trial uses another
  (UACR 3 mg/mmol = 30 mg/g; HbA1c in mmol/mol -> %; LDL 1.8 mmol/L = 70 mg/dL).
- Condition and medication names are short lowercase generic names ("type 2 diabetes",
  "heart failure", "kidney transplant", "spironolactone"). Use `in` with a list for "any of"
  ("Current treatment with other MRAs (e.g. spironolactone, eplerenone)").
- A lab or vital qualified only by when it is measured ("at screening", "within past 12
  months", "on screening labs") still gets a predicate: the patient's latest value is used.
- Set `predicate` to null when the criterion needs a time window or duration on an event,
  diagnosis or treatment ("MI within 60 days", "for at least 3 months"), a severity grade or class the fields can't hold, a trend,
  investigator judgment, consent or logistics, a field not listed above, or an unstated
  threshold ("hypotension", "good nutritional status"). Do not invent thresholds.
- Never write a predicate that only partly captures the criterion. If in doubt, use null.

1. Subject has provided written informed consent by signing the study Informed Consent Form (ICF) prior to any clinical investigation-related procedure

4. NYHA Class IIIB or NYHA Class IV
5. Subject has ≥ 1 Heart Failure Hospitalization in the last 12 months
6. Subject is already implanted with a CardioMEMS PA Sensor OR willing to undergo a CardioMEMS PA Sensor implant
7. Subject is willing and able to be implanted with the HM3 LVAS if randomized to HM3 Group

Randomization Criteria:

1. Subject has been implanted with a CardioMEMS PA Sensor for at least 90 days.
2. Subject is receiving guideline directed medical therapy with optimal doses (or documented medication contraindication or intolerance) of betablockers, Angiotensin-Converting-Enzyme-inhibitors or Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers or angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (if eligible), Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists, Sodium-Glucose co-Transporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, and diuretics for at least 30 of the last 90 days.
3. mean PAP ≥ 30 mmHg.
4. The subject will not be randomized if they have any other factor that represents inordinate risk for either continued GDMT or LVAD implant.

Single Arm Registry Criteria:

1. Subject has received a CardioMEMS PA Sensor implant following enrollment in the trial.
2. Subject is receiving guideline directed medical therapy with optimal doses (or documented medication contraindication or intolerance) of betablockers, Angiotensin-Converting-Enzyme-inhibitors or Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers or angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (if eligible), Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists, Sodium-Glucose co-Transporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, and diuretics for at least 30 of the last 90 days.
3. mean PAP <30 mmHg

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Subject is < 18 years of age at the time of informed consent.
2. Dependent on IV inotrope in the last 30 days.
3. Contra-indications to HM3 LVAS or CardioMEMS HF system.
4. Etiology of HF due to or associated with uncorrected thyroid disease, obstructive cardiomyopathy, pericardial disease, amyloidosis, or restrictive cardiomyopathy.
5. Technical obstacles to LVAD or CardioMEMS implantation which pose an inordinately high surgical risk, in the judgment of the implanter.
6. Existence of ongoing MCS.
7. Presence of mechanical aortic valve that will not be either converted to a bioprosthesis or oversewn at the time of LVAD implant.
8. History of any solid organ transplant.
9. Psychiatric disease/disorder, irreversible cognitive dysfunction or psychosocial issues that are likely to impair compliance with the study protocol and LVAS management.
10. Presence of an active, uncontrolled infection.
11. Complex congenital heart disease.
12. Currently Pregnant or capable of becoming Pregnant and Unwilling to Use Contraception with LVAD.
13. History of pulmonary embolism within 30 days prior to enrollment or history of recurrent (>1 episode) pulmonary embolism and/or deep vein thrombosis.
14. Planned VAD or Bi-VAD support prior to enrollment.
15. Presence of any one of the following risk factors for or indications of severe end organ dysfunction or failure:

    1. An INR ≥ 2.0 not due to anticoagulation therapy
    2. An eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 and nonresponsive to diuretic therapy or receiving chronic dialysis.
    3. Biopsy proven liver cirrhosis.
    4. Need for chronic renal replacement therapy.
    5. History of severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) defined by Forced Expiratory Volume FEV1 < 30% predicted.
    6. History of cerebrovascular disease with significant (> 80%) uncorrected internal carotid stenosis.
    7. Significant peripheral vascular disease (PVD) accompanied by ischemic rest pain or extremity ulceration.
16. Any condition other than HF that could limit survival to less than 24 months.
17. Participation in any other clinical investigation with an active treatment arm that is likely to confound study results or affect the study outcome.

  "Other protocol-defined criteria apply" or "None".

### Outcome

`outcome` is relative to eligibility, never to the literal wording of the criterion:

- `pass`: the patient is fine on this criterion. For an inclusion, the patient meets it. For an
  exclusion, the excluding condition does not apply to the patient.
- `fail`: the criterion disqualifies the patient. For an inclusion, the patient clearly does not
  meet it. For an exclusion, the excluding condition applies.
- `unknown`: the note and facts don't say enough to decide. Missing data is always `unknown`,
  never `fail`. A condition that is simply not mentioned is `unknown`, not absent; only an
  explicit statement ("no history of pancreatitis", "denies tobacco") counts as evidence.

Criteria that only the study team can decide (informed consent, willingness to comply,
investigator judgment, study logistics) are `unknown`.

### Quotes

Code checks both quotes against their sources and discards your verdict if either is not
found, so copy them character for character. Never paraphrase, summarize, fix typos, join
pieces from different places, or add words of your own.

  criterion. Usually the criterion text itself.
- `patient_evidence`: a contiguous span of the patient note, or one line of the patient facts
  copied exactly as listed (for example `labs.egfr: 48 mL/min/1.73m2 (2026-10-02)`). Use the
  shortest span that supports your outcome. Required for `pass` and `fail`. Use null only for

what the record shows, and why that gives the outcome.

Trial: NCT06526195

<eligibility_text>
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Subject has provided written informed consent by signing the study Informed Consent Form (ICF) prior to any clinical investigation-related procedure
2. LVEF ≤30% and Cardiac Index ≤ 2.5 L/min/m²
3. Limited functional status as demonstrated by 6MWT ≤ 350 m due to HF related reasons OR peak VO2 ≤ 14 mL/kg/min (or <50% of predicted peak VO2 value)

5. Subject has ≥ 1 Heart Failure Hospitalization in the last 12 months
6. Subject is already implanted with a CardioMEMS PA Sensor OR willing to undergo a CardioMEMS PA Sensor implant
7. Subject is willing and able to be implanted with the HM3 LVAS if randomized to HM3 Group

Randomization Criteria:

1. Subject has been implanted with a CardioMEMS PA Sensor for at least 90 days.
2. 3. mean PAP ≥ 30 mmHg.
4. The subject will not be randomized if they have any other factor that represents inordinate risk for either continued GDMT or LVAD implant.

Single Arm Registry Criteria:

1. Subject has received a CardioMEMS PA Sensor implant following enrollment in the trial.
2. Subject is receiving guideline directed medical therapy with optimal doses (or documented medication contraindication or intolerance) of betablockers, Angiotensin-Converting-Enzyme-inhibitors or Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers or angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (if eligible), Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists, Sodium-Glucose co-Transporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, and diuretics for at least 30 of the last 90 days.
3. mean PAP <30 mmHg

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Subject is < 18 years of age at the time of informed consent.
2. Dependent on IV inotrope in the last 30 days.
3. Contra-indications to HM3 LVAS or CardioMEMS HF system.
4. Etiology of HF due to or associated with uncorrected thyroid disease, obstructive cardiomyopathy, pericardial disease, amyloidosis, or restrictive cardiomyopathy.
5. Technical obstacles to LVAD or CardioMEMS implantation which pose an inordinately high surgical risk, in the judgment of the implanter.
6. Existence of ongoing MCS.
7. Presence of mechanical aortic valve that will not be either converted to a bioprosthesis or oversewn at the time of LVAD implant.
8. History of any solid organ transplant.
9. Psychiatric disease/disorder, irreversible cognitive dysfunction or psychosocial issues that are likely to impair compliance with the study protocol and LVAS management.
10. Presence of an active, uncontrolled infection.
11. Complex congenital heart disease.
12. Currently Pregnant or capable of becoming Pregnant and Unwilling to Use Contraception with LVAD.
13. History of pulmonary embolism within 30 days prior to enrollment or history of recurrent (>1 episode) pulmonary embolism and/or deep vein thrombosis.
14. Planned VAD or Bi-VAD support prior to enrollment.
15. Presence of any one of the following risk factors for or indications of severe end organ dysfunction or failure:

    6. History of cerebrovascular disease with significant (> 80%) uncorrected internal carotid stenosis.
    7. Significant peripheral vascular disease (PVD) accompanied by ischemic rest pain or extremity ulceration.

17. Participation in any other clinical investigation with an active treatment arm that is likely to confound study results or affect the study outcome.

You compile the free-text eligibility criteria of a clinical trial into atomic, structured
criteria that code can evaluate against a patient record. Answer with one JSON object matching
the `CompiledCriteria` schema, nothing else.

### Splitting

- One criterion is one independently checkable condition. A bullet that joins independent
  conditions ("A, B, or C" in an exclusion list; "A and B" in an inclusion list) becomes one
  criterion per condition.
- Keep alternatives together when they are one requirement ("eGFR 30-60 OR UACR >= 30 mg/g"
  in an inclusion list is a single criterion that needs judgment).
- A numeric range ("HbA1c 6.5 to 10%") becomes two criteria, one per bound, both quoting the
  same text.
- `type` is `inclusion` or `exclusion`, from the section the line sits in.
- `text` is copied verbatim from the trial, character for character: a contiguous span of the
  given text, without the bullet marker or numbering. Never paraphrase, fix typos, or join
  pieces from different places.
- Skip section headers, notes about how labs are measured, enrolment caps, and lines such as
  "Other protocol-defined criteria apply" or "None".
- Skip criteria that only restate the minimum age, maximum age or sex ("Children", "Age 18
  years and older"): those come from the trial's structured fields.
- Skip criteria for participants who are not patients (providers, pharmacists, caregivers).

### Categories

- `demographic`: age, sex, language, location, social situation.
- `diagnosis`: a disease or condition the patient has or must not have.
- `lab`: a laboratory value or vital sign threshold.
- `medication`: current, past or planned drugs, allergies to drugs.
- `history`: past events (prior MI, prior surgery, prior episodes) and time-bound history.
- `procedure`: procedures, devices, transplants, dialysis, imaging.
- `other`: consent, compliance, investigator judgment, study logistics.

### Predicates

Write a `predicate` only when the criterion can be checked from these patient fields alone:

- `age` (years): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number
- `sex`: == with "female" or "male"
- `pregnant`, `smoker`: == with "true" or "false"
- `conditions`, `meds`: `has` / `not_has` with one lowercase name, or `in` with a list of names (any of them)
- `labs.hba1c` (%), `labs.egfr` (mL/min/1.73m2), `labs.uacr` (mg/g), `labs.upcr` (mg/g), `labs.potassium` (mmol/L), `labs.ldl` (mg/dL), `labs.creatinine` (mg/dL), `labs.albumin` (g/dL), `labs.alt` (U/L), `labs.hscrp` (mg/L), `labs.fvc_pct` (% predicted), `labs.fev1_pct` (% predicted), `labs.fev1_fvc` (ratio), `labs.svc_pct` (% predicted), `labs.dlco_pct` (% predicted), `labs.alsfrs_r` (points), `labs.six_mwd` (m), `labs.pvr` (WU), `labs.pcwp` (mmHg): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number in that unit
- `vitals.bmi` (kg/m2), `vitals.sbp` (mmHg), `vitals.dbp` (mmHg), `vitals.weight` (kg): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number in that unit

Rules:

- The predicate states the criterion as written: it is true when the criterion's condition
  holds for the patient. For an exclusion ("Type 1 diabetes") that means
  `{"field": "conditions", "op": "has", "value": "type 1 diabetes"}`; code inverts
  exclusions, you never do.
- Use the canonical unit listed for each lab and vital and convert when the trial uses another
  (UACR 3 mg/mmol = 30 mg/g; HbA1c in mmol/mol -> %; LDL 1.8 mmol/L = 70 mg/dL).
- Condition and medication names are short lowercase generic names ("type 2 diabetes",
  "heart failure", "kidney transplant", "spironolactone"). Use `in` with a list for "any of"
  ("Current treatment with other MRAs (e.g. spironolactone, eplerenone)").
- A lab or vital qualified only by when it is measured ("at screening", "within past 12
  months", "on screening labs") still gets a predicate: the patient's latest value is used.
- Set `predicate` to null when the criterion needs a time window or duration on an event,
  diagnosis or treatment ("MI within 60 days", "for at least 3 months"), a severity grade or class the fields can't hold, a trend,
  investigator judgment, consent or logistics, a field not listed above, or an unstated
  threshold ("hypotension", "good nutritional status"). Do not invent thresholds.
- Never write a predicate that only partly captures the criterion. If in doubt, use null.

You compile the free-text eligibility criteria of a clinical trial into atomic, structured
criteria that code can evaluate against a patient record. Answer with one JSON object matching
the `CompiledCriteria` schema, nothing else.

### Splitting

- One criterion is one independently checkable condition. A bullet that joins independent
  conditions ("A, B, or C" in an exclusion list; "A and B" in an inclusion list) becomes one
  criterion per condition.
- Keep alternatives together when they are one requirement ("eGFR 30-60 OR UACR >= 30 mg/g"
  in an inclusion list is a single criterion that needs judgment).
- A numeric range ("HbA1c 6.5 to 10%") becomes two criteria, one per bound, both quoting the
  same text.
- `type` is `inclusion` or `exclusion`, from the section the line sits in.
- `text` is copied verbatim from the trial, character for character: a contiguous span of the
  given text, without the bullet marker or numbering. Never paraphrase, fix typos, or join
  pieces from different places.
- Skip section headers, notes about how labs are measured, enrolment caps, and lines such as
  "Other protocol-defined criteria apply" or "None".
- Skip criteria that only restate the minimum age, maximum age or sex ("Children", "Age 18
  years and older"): those come from the trial's structured fields.
- Skip criteria for participants who are not patients (providers, pharmacists, caregivers).

### Categories

- `demographic`: age, sex, language, location, social situation.
- `diagnosis`: a disease or condition the patient has or must not have.
- `lab`: a laboratory value or vital sign threshold.
- `medication`: current, past or planned drugs, allergies to drugs.
- `history`: past events (prior MI, prior surgery, prior episodes) and time-bound history.
- `procedure`: procedures, devices, transplants, dialysis, imaging.
- `other`: consent, compliance, investigator judgment, study logistics.

### Predicates

Write a `predicate` only when the criterion can be checked from these patient fields alone:

- `age` (years): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number
- `sex`: == with "female" or "male"
- `pregnant`, `smoker`: == with "true" or "false"
- `conditions`, `meds`: `has` / `not_has` with one lowercase name, or `in` with a list of names (any of them)
- `labs.hba1c` (%), `labs.egfr` (mL/min/1.73m2), `labs.uacr` (mg/g), `labs.upcr` (mg/g), `labs.potassium` (mmol/L), `labs.ldl` (mg/dL), `labs.creatinine` (mg/dL), `labs.albumin` (g/dL), `labs.alt` (U/L), `labs.hscrp` (mg/L), `labs.fvc_pct` (% predicted), `labs.fev1_pct` (% predicted), `labs.fev1_fvc` (ratio), `labs.svc_pct` (% predicted), `labs.dlco_pct` (% predicted), `labs.alsfrs_r` (points), `labs.six_mwd` (m), `labs.pvr` (WU), `labs.pcwp` (mmHg): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number in that unit
- `vitals.bmi` (kg/m2), `vitals.sbp` (mmHg), `vitals.dbp` (mmHg), `vitals.weight` (kg): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number in that unit

Rules:

- The predicate states the criterion as written: it is true when the criterion's condition
  holds for the patient. For an exclusion ("Type 1 diabetes") that means
  `{"field": "conditions", "op": "has", "value": "type 1 diabetes"}`; code inverts
  exclusions, you never do.
- Use the canonical unit listed for each lab and vital and convert when the trial uses another
  (UACR 3 mg/mmol = 30 mg/g; HbA1c in mmol/mol -> %; LDL 1.8 mmol/L = 70 mg/dL).
- Condition and medication names are short lowercase generic names ("type 2 diabetes",
  "heart failure", "kidney transplant", "spironolactone"). Use `in` with a list for "any of"
  ("Current treatment with other MRAs (e.g. spironolactone, eplerenone)").
- A lab or vital qualified only by when it is measured ("at screening", "within past 12
  months", "on screening labs") still gets a predicate: the patient's latest value is used.
- Set `predicate` to null when the criterion needs a time window or duration on an event,
  diagnosis or treatment ("MI within 60 days", "for at least 3 months"), a severity grade or class the fields can't hold, a trend,
  investigator judgment, consent or logistics, a field not listed above, or an unstated
  threshold ("hypotension", "good nutritional status"). Do not invent thresholds.
- Never write a predicate that only partly captures the criterion. If in doubt, use null.

You compile the free-text eligibility criteria of a clinical trial into atomic, structured
criteria that code can evaluate against a patient record. Answer with one JSON object matching
the `CompiledCriteria` schema, nothing else.

### Splitting

- One criterion is one independently checkable condition. A bullet that joins independent
  conditions ("A, B, or C" in an exclusion list; "A and B" in an inclusion list) becomes one
  criterion per condition.
- Keep alternatives together when they are one requirement ("eGFR 30-60 OR UACR >= 30 mg/g"
  in an inclusion list is a single criterion that needs judgment).
- A numeric range ("HbA1c 6.5 to 10%") becomes two criteria, one per bound, both quoting the
  same text.
- `type` is `inclusion` or `exclusion`, from the section the line sits in.
- `text` is copied verbatim from the trial, character for character: a contiguous span of the
  given text, without the bullet marker or numbering. Never paraphrase, fix typos, or join
  pieces from different places.
- Skip section headers, notes about how labs are measured, enrolment caps, and lines such as
  "Other protocol-defined criteria apply" or "None".
- Skip criteria that only restate the minimum age, maximum age or sex ("Children", "Age 18
  years and older"): those come from the trial's structured fields.
- Skip criteria for participants who are not patients (providers, pharmacists, caregivers).

### Categories

- `demographic`: age, sex, language, location, social situation.
- `diagnosis`: a disease or condition the patient has or must not have.
- `lab`: a laboratory value or vital sign threshold.
- `medication`: current, past or planned drugs, allergies to drugs.
- `history`: past events (prior MI, prior surgery, prior episodes) and time-bound history.
- `procedure`: procedures, devices, transplants, dialysis, imaging.
- `other`: consent, compliance, investigator judgment, study logistics.

### Predicates

Write a `predicate` only when the criterion can be checked from these patient fields alone:

- `age` (years): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number
- `sex`: == with "female" or "male"
- `pregnant`, `smoker`: == with "true" or "false"
- `conditions`, `meds`: `has` / `not_has` with one lowercase name, or `in` with a list of names (any of them)
- `labs.hba1c` (%), `labs.egfr` (mL/min/1.73m2), `labs.uacr` (mg/g), `labs.upcr` (mg/g), `labs.potassium` (mmol/L), `labs.ldl` (mg/dL), `labs.creatinine` (mg/dL), `labs.albumin` (g/dL), `labs.alt` (U/L), `labs.hscrp` (mg/L), `labs.fvc_pct` (% predicted), `labs.fev1_pct` (% predicted), `labs.fev1_fvc` (ratio), `labs.svc_pct` (% predicted), `labs.dlco_pct` (% predicted), `labs.alsfrs_r` (points), `labs.six_mwd` (m), `labs.pvr` (WU), `labs.pcwp` (mmHg): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number in that unit
- `vitals.bmi` (kg/m2), `vitals.sbp` (mmHg), `vitals.dbp` (mmHg), `vitals.weight` (kg): >=, <=, >, <, == with a number in that unit

Rules:

- The predicate states the criterion as written: it is true when the criterion's condition
  holds for the patient. For an exclusion ("Type 1 diabetes") that means
  `{"field": "conditions", "op": "has", "value": "type 1 diabetes"}`; code inverts
  exclusions, you never do.
- Use the canonical unit listed for each lab and vital and convert when the trial uses another
  (UACR 3 mg/mmol = 30 mg/g; HbA1c in mmol/mol -> %; LDL 1.8 mmol/L = 70 mg/dL).
- Condition and medication names are short lowercase generic names ("type 2 diabetes",
  "heart failure", "kidney transplant", "spironolactone"). Use `in` with a list for "any of"
  ("Current treatment with other MRAs (e.g. spironolactone, eplerenone)").
- A lab or vital qualified only by when it is measured ("at screening", "within past 12
  months", "on screening labs") still gets a predicate: the patient's latest value is used.
- Set `predicate` to null when the criterion needs a time window or duration on an event,
  diagnosis or treatment ("MI within 60 days", "for at least 3 months"), a severity grade or class the fields can't hold, a trend,
  investigator judgment, consent or logistics, a field not listed above, or an unstated
  threshold ("hypotension", "good nutritional status"). Do not invent thresholds.
- Never write a predicate that only partly captures the criterion. If in doubt, use null.

Trial: NCT06526195

<eligibility_text>
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Subject has provided written informed consent by signing the study Informed Consent Form (ICF) prior to any clinical investigation-related procedure
2. LVEF ≤30% and Cardiac Index ≤ 2.5 L/min/m²
3. Limited functional status as demonstrated by 6MWT ≤ 350 m due to HF related reasons OR peak VO2 ≤ 14 mL/kg/min (or <50% of predicted peak VO2 value)
4. NYHA Class IIIB or NYHA Class IV
5. Subject has ≥ 1 Heart Failure Hospitalization in the last 12 months
6. Subject is already implanted with a CardioMEMS PA Sensor OR willing to undergo a CardioMEMS PA Sensor implant
7. Subject is willing and able to be implanted with the HM3 LVAS if randomized to HM3 Group

Randomization Criteria:

1. Subject has been implanted with a CardioMEMS PA Sensor for at least 90 days.
2. Subject is receiving guideline directed medical therapy with optimal doses (or documented medication contraindication or intolerance) of betablockers, Angiotensin-Converting-Enzyme-inhibitors or Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers or angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (if eligible), Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists, Sodium-Glucose co-Transporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, and diuretics for at least 30 of the last 90 days.
3. mean PAP ≥ 30 mmHg.
4. The subject will not be randomized if they have any other factor that represents inordinate risk for either continued GDMT or LVAD implant.

Single Arm Registry Criteria:

1. Subject has received a CardioMEMS PA Sensor implant following enrollment in the trial.
2. Subject is receiving guideline directed medical therapy with optimal doses (or documented medication contraindication or intolerance) of betablockers, Angiotensin-Converting-Enzyme-inhibitors or Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers or angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (if eligible), Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists, Sodium-Glucose co-Transporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, and diuretics for at least 30 of the last 90 days.
3. mean PAP <30 mmHg

1. Subject is < 18 years of age at the time of informed consent.
2. Dependent on IV inotrope in the last 30 days.
3. Contra-indications to HM3 LVAS or CardioMEMS HF system.

5. Technical obstacles to LVAD or CardioMEMS implantation which pose an inordinately high surgical risk, in the judgment of the implanter.
6. Existence of ongoing MCS.
7. Presence of mechanical aortic valve that will not be either converted to a bioprosthesis or oversewn at the time of LVAD implant.
8. History of any solid organ transplant.
9. Psychiatric disease/disorder, irreversible cognitive dysfunction or psychosocial issues that are likely to impair compliance with the study protocol and LVAS management.
10. Presence of an active, uncontrolled infection.
11. Complex congenital heart disease.
12. Currently Pregnant or capable of becoming Pregnant and Unwilling to Use Contraception with LVAD.
13. History of pulmonary embolism within 30 days prior to enrollment or history of recurrent (>1 episode) pulmonary embolism and/or deep vein thrombosis.
14. Planned VAD or Bi-VAD support prior to enrollment.

    1. An INR ≥ 2.0 not due to anticoagulation therapy
    2. An eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 and nonresponsive to diuretic therapy or receiving chronic dialysis.
    3. Biopsy proven liver cirrhosis.
    4. Need for chronic renal replacement therapy.
    5. History of severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) defined by Forced Expiratory Volume FEV1 < 30% predicted.
    6. History of cerebrovascular disease with significant (> 80%) uncorrected internal carotid stenosis.
    7. Significant peripheral vascular disease (PVD) accompanied by ischemic rest pain or extremity ulceration.
16. Any condition other than HF that could limit survival to less than 24 months.
17. Participation in any other clinical investigation with an active treatment arm that is likely to confound study results or affect the study outcome.

Trial: NCT05587712

<eligibility_text>
Inclusion Criteria

* Documented, historic diagnostic right heart catheterization (RHC) any time before Screening confirming the diagnosis of PAH WHO Group 1 in any of the following subtypes:
* Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH)
* Heritable PAH
* Drug/toxin-induced PAH
* PAH associated with connective tissue disease
* PAH-congenital heart disease (CHD) with shunt closure >6 months before Screening and subsequently confirmed by RHC before Screening
* PAH with coincidental shunt.
* Must be on a stable dose(s) of background PAH therapy (phosphdiesterase-5 (PDE5) inhibitors, endothelin receptor antagonists (ERAs), soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators (sGCS), or prostanoids [including subcutaneous and intravenous])
* If male, agree to the following during the intervention period and for at least 16 weeks (112 days) after the last dose of study intervention:
* Abstains from heterosexual intercourse as their preferred and usual lifestyle (abstinent on a long-term and persistent basis) and agrees to remain abstinent or
* Uses contraception unless confirmed to be azoospermic (vasectomized or secondary to medical cause, documented from the site personnel's review of the participant's medical records, medical examination, or medical history interview) as detailed below:
* Uses a male condom plus partner use of an additional contraceptive method when having penile-vaginal intercourse with a woman of childbearing potential (WOCBP) who is not currently pregnant Note: Men with a pregnant or breastfeeding partner must agree to remain abstinent from penile-vaginal intercourse or use a male condom during each episode of penile-vaginal penetration.
* If female, must be either not a WOCBP or use a contraceptive method that is highly effective or be abstinent from heterosexual intercourse during the intervention period and for at least 16 weeks (112 days) after the last dose of study intervention
* If male, agrees to refrain from donating blood or sperm for the duration of the study and for 16 weeks (112 days) after the last dose of study intervention
* If female, agrees to refrain from donating blood, eggs, or ovum for the duration of the study and for at least 16 weeks (112 days) after the last dose of study intervention

Exclusion Criteria

* History of left-sided heart disease, including valvular disease (eg, moderate or greater mitral or aortic regurgitation or stenosis), left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, and/or left heart failure (eg, restrictive or dilated cardiomyopathy)
* Severe (as based on the opinion of the investigator) congenital or developmental abnormalities of the lung, thorax, and/or diaphragm
* History of Eisenmenger syndrome, Potts shunt, or atrial septostomy
* Unrepaired or residual cardiac shunt
* Diagnosis of pulmonary veno-occlusive diseases, pulmonary capillary hemangiomatosis, or overt signs of capillary and/or venous involvement
* PAH associated with portal hypertension
* Known visceral (lung, liver, or brain) arteriovenous malformation(s)
* History of full or partial pneumonectomy
* Untreated more than mild obstructive sleep apnea
* History of known pericardial constriction
* Family history of sudden cardiac death or long QT syndrome
* Any current or prior history of symptomatic coronary disease (myocardial infarction, percutaneous coronary intervention, coronary artery bypass graft surgery, or cardiac anginal chest pain) within 6 months before Screening
* Cerebrovascular accident within 3 months before Screening
* Prior exposure to sotatercept or luspatercept or has had an allergic reaction to any of their excipients
</eligibility_text>
